AFDRIW

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Riverton WY
1011 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- The next weather system continues to move into the area
  tonight, bringing widespread snow across the mountains of 
  western and central Wyoming. Winter Storms Warnings/Weather 
  Advisories are in effect through Saturday afternoon.

- Lower elevations east of the Divide, temperatures remain mild
  ahead of a cold front. Colder temperatures arrive tonight,
  with colder temps and chances for light snow Saturday morning
  behind the cold front.

- Temperatures remain cooler through the weekend with slight
  warming trend into next week. Another weak system for Sunday
  night into Monday morning for western mountains, and again
  Thursday night but otherwise, most will remain dry.

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 1200 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

IR continues to show the ample cloud cover increasing from the 
west from the main upper level low over the Pacific northwest. 
The PFJ evident on WV has maintained its strength with the 
northwest flow across the northern Rockies as it starts to sag 
further south. This will pull in the Pacific moisture and bring 
the mountain snow and next cold front through the CWA Saturday 
morning. Snow totals in the higher elevations is similar to the 
previous model run, but a bit higher across the Cody/Bighorn 
Foothills. As such, for the Cody area, a winter weather advisory
has been issued due to 2 to 4 inches and gusty winds expected 
ahead of FROPA from after midnight through much of Saturday 
morning to cover morning travel for the weekend after holiday 
commute. Gusty winds ahead of the system continue to strengthen 
through the afternoon, peaking across the wind corridor towards
sunset and overnight where gusts up to 50-60 mph are likely 
from eastern Sweetwater to South Pass and into southern Natrona 
County. This will subside by mid to late morning post FROPA. 

The system continues to be progressive, and will quickly push 
out through Saturday afternoon with improving sky conditions and
diminishing snowfall. Induced ridging into Sunday with the next
shortwave Sunday night but weaker due to decreased divergence
aloft and weakened PFJ. The main upper level low will skirt well
to the south by Thursday with minimal snow chances for higher
elevations but most of the CWA will remain dry post Saturday
morning and into much of next work week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 101 AM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

Convective banding already starting to pick up on radar this
morning, with snow spreading across Jackson Hole and over
Togwotee Pass currently. The northwest flow will continue
producing scattered snow with the leading edge of the lifting
aloft, but snowfall rates in the western mountains will be
fairly low into this afternoon. Once the next trough and
associated jet max sweep in starting around sunset tonight,
better lifting and moisture will result in quicker and more
productive snowfall production, and this activity will also 
spread into the Bighorns after sunset. The peak snowfall 
production will generally occur between midnight tonight and 
noon Saturday. Overall snow amount forecast has not changed 
noticeably, so current alignment of Winter Storm Warnings and 
Advisories will not need adjustments with this package. 

As the trough sweeps through overnight, an associated cold front
will race southward for areas east of the Divide, bringing
colder temperatures back into the region. As it pivots through,
a band of snow showers will sweep across east of the Divide, 
bringing a brief band of snowfall to the Bighorn and Wind River 
Basins and across Johnson and Natrona Counties. Since the system
is moving through quickly, the period of snowfall will be 
brief, but some accumulations are expected, ranging from a trace
to one inch for most of the Wind River and Bighorn Basins, to 
one to two inches for Johnson and Natrona Counties downwind from
the Bighorn Range. By noon or so on Saturday, the system will 
be well to the southeast, and all snowfall production will be 
complete, both higher and lower elevation. Daytime highs will be
dependent on how much snow stick to surfaces, but highs will 
struggle to get into the 30s east of the Divide. Most of the 
Green River Basin and Sweetwater County will miss out on this 
system, so highs will push back into the low to mid 40s on 
Saturday.

Behind this system, broad H5 ridging return across the Rockies.
Temperatures Sunday will again hover in the 30s for most areas,
with warmer temperatures along the I-80 corridor. The broad
trough off the West Coast will eject into Canada on Monday. The
tail end of this system will clip western Wyoming, bringing
another round of snow to the western mountains. As flow from
this system will be more form the southwest, and moisture will
be more limited, snowfall amounts Monday will be low.

The general trend into next week will be temperatures near
normal, while the main storm track sets up farther to the south
across the Four Corners region.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 1010 PM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

WEST OF THE DIVIDE...KBPI/KJAC/KPNA/KRKS TERMINALS.

Precipitation and MVFR to IFR conditions continue tonight into 
Saturday morning. Rain will change over to all snow at 
KJAC/KBPI/KPNA tonight before sunrise Saturday. This changeover will 
occur at KRKS around 16Z Saturday. Snow will abruptly end from north 
to south Saturday morning into Saturday afternoon. Some snow showers 
may linger near KRKS Saturday afternoon as the cold front stalls 
just west of KRKS. A heavy snow band associated with the cold front 
will pass through Saturday morning with brief reductions to LIFR 
possible (30%) as it passes through. Strong wind will accompany the 
cold frontal passage and possibly (30%) result in a short period of 
BLSN at KJAC. Other terminals may have some BLSN, but the chance is 
too low (15%) due to lesser snow amounts expected at those 
terminals. Mountain obscuration will be prevalent through most of 
Saturday morning improving from north to south from Saturday morning 
through Saturday afternoon.


EAST OF THE DIVIDE...KCOD/KCPR/KLND/KRIW/KWRL TERMINALS.

Snow begins at KCOD to start the period and will push south tonight 
into Saturday morning. Precipitation may start as a rain/snow mix at 
KWRL initially tonight and at KRIW early Saturday morning before 
changing over to all snow Saturday morning. Conditions will 
generally range from MVFR to IFR once snow begins tonight/Saturday 
morning. Brief reductions to LIFR may occur as a heavy snow band 
pushes through Saturday morning. Strong wind associated with a cold 
frontal passage will result in patchy blowing snow, especially at 
KCOD, KRIW, and KCPR Saturday morning into Saturday afternoon. 
Mountain obscuration will be prevalent through most of Saturday 
morning improving from north to south from Saturday morning through 
Saturday afternoon.

Please see the Aviation Weather Center and/or CWSU ZDV and ZLC for 
the latest information on smoke, icing, and turbulence forecasts.

&&

.RIW WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
Winter Storm Warning until 11 AM MST Saturday for WYZ001-002-
012-014-015-024-025.

Winter Weather Advisory until 11 AM MST Saturday for WYZ003.

Winter Weather Advisory until 5 PM MST Saturday for WYZ008-009.

High Wind Warning until 11 AM MST Saturday for WYZ019.

&&

$$

alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 28 at 12:16AM MST until November 28 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Riverton WY
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 12 and
20 inches at higher elevations. Portions of the Upper Green River
Basin Foothills will see accumulations of 8 to 12 inches. Winds
gusting up to 50 to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of central, northwest, and west central Wyoming.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult, especially across Teton
Pass and Togwotee Pass.
